America) (country ZW) or the United States (country US), or how that price has changed over the last year. Returns the official average or median shop price that the national statistics office publishes for a standard item, built from the shelf prices its price collectors record in shops for the consumer price index (shelf prices observed by price collectors, not receipts and not what one shopper paid; some offices also use retailers' scanner data), with the exact item definition (for example 'Full-fat milk, per 2 litres'), the unit, the reference month, the change on a year earlier where the office publishes comparable figures (an answer carries none where the office advises against comparing months), the official source and licence. Each country defines its own standard items, so the item definition in the answer matters and related definitions are listed. How fresh: Canada: monthly, not live: Statistics Canada publishes each month's averages about five weeks after the month ends (August 2026 was released on 7 October 2026), and every answer states its reference month; the United Kingdom: monthly: ONS publishes each month's file about three to four weeks after the month ends (August 2026 appeared in late September); our copy is refreshed daily and each answer states its reference month; Hong Kong: daily; Ireland: monthly, published with the Consumer Price Index (usually the second week of the following month); each answer states its reference month; Latvia: monthly, usually in the second week of the following month; each answer states its reference month; Mexico (Profeco shelf prices): monthly, about 7 weeks behind; Malaysia (shop shelf prices, DOSM PriceCatcher): DOSM refreshes the monthly file daily; our copy is refreshed daily and each answer names the newest price date; countries WFP surveys (Africa, Asia, Middle East, Latin America): WFP files are updated about monthly (HDX file last modified 2026-10-12); the newest observation in a country is often 1 to 5 months old; our copy is refreshed daily; the United States: monthly: BLS releases the new month about the 10th to 14th of the following month; our copy is refreshed daily and each answer states its reference month. This is a published national (or regional) average, not a range of individual transactions, so the range fields can be null. Do not use for the price at a particular supermarket or online shop, loyalty-card or special-offer prices, restaurant meals, petrol or diesel, or for other countries.

country.description: CA = Canada (Statistics Canada: monthly average retail prices of 110 selected products, national and provincial, official statistic, not a live price); GB = United Kingdom (Office for National Statistics: median shop prices of about 200 grocery and drink product types, monthly, UK and 12 regions and nations); HK = Hong Kong; IE = Ireland (Central Statistics Office: national average shop prices of about 76 standard items, monthly); LV = Latvia (Central Statistical Bureau: national average shop prices of about 130 food and drink items, monthly); MX = Mexico; MY = Malaysia; Countries as ISO codes: AF = Afghanistan, AM = Armenia, BD = Bangladesh, BF = Burkina Faso, BI = Burundi, BJ = Benin, BO = Bolivia, CD = Democratic Republic of the Congo, CF = Central African Republic, CI = Cote d'Ivoire, CM = Cameroon, DJ = Djibouti, ET = Ethiopia, GM = Gambia, GN = Guinea, GW = Guinea-Bissau, HT = Haiti, ID = Indonesia, IN = India, IQ = Iraq, JO = Jordan, KG = Kyrgyzstan, LA = Laos, LB = Lebanon, LR = Liberia, LS = Lesotho, ML = Mali, MM = Myanmar, MR = Mauritania, MW = Malawi, MZ = Mozambique, NE = Niger, NG = Nigeria, NP = Nepal, PH = Philippines, PK = Pakistan, RW = Rwanda, SD = Sudan, SL = Sierra Leone, SN = Senegal, SO = Somalia, SS = South Sudan, TD = Chad, TG = Togo, TL = Timor-Leste, TZ = Tanzania, UA = Ukraine, UG = Uganda, YE = Yemen, ZW = Zimbabwe. World Food Programme market surveys of staple foods; a country with no recent survey of 5 or more markets answers 'no matches'.; US = United States (Bureau of Labor Statistics: average retail prices of about 45 standard food and drink items, monthly, national and four regions)

item.description: Everyday item in plain words, e.g. 'milk', 'white bread', 'eggs', 'butter', 'coffee', 'bananas', 'beer'. Each country measures its own standard pack or cut; the answer names it and lists other definitions. Canada: Statistics Canada's 110 standard products, each in one standard size, e.g. milk, 1 litre milk, 4 litre milk, soy milk, nut milk, cream, butter, margarine, cheese, yogurt, eggs, ground beef, steak, sirloin. Milk is published per 1, 2 and 4 litres (2 litres by default); the answer names the exact product and lists the other sizes. GB: ONS's product types, each in one pack size, e.g. eggs (free-range, pack of 12), milk (whole, 4 pints), semi-skimmed milk (2 pints), bread (sliced white, 800 g), butter (250 g), cheese (cheddar, per kg), chicken (whole, per kg), beef mince (per kg), bananas, apples, potatoes (per kg), rice, pasta, instant coffee, tea bags, sugar, lager, wine. HK: a grocery category in English ('milk', 'eggs', 'rice', 'bread', 'honey', 'peanut butter', 'instant noodles', 'cooking oil', 'beer'). The answer is the median and range of shelf prices of the products in that category (brands and pack sizes differ), per kg or per litre where the pack size is known, otherwise per pack; it names the category and lists related ones. IE: the CSO's standard items, e.g. milk (full-fat, 2 litres), white bread (800 g sliced pan), eggs (large, half dozen), butter (per lb), cheese (Irish cheddar), chicken (whole bird), bananas, potatoes, sugar, tea bags, beer (can of lager), wine (75 cl), whiskey, pint of stout or lager (bar). The CSO has no coffee, mince or cereal. LV: the CSB's standard items, e.g. milk (1 l), bread (wheat, 1 kg; also rye bread), eggs (10), butter (1 kg), cheese (1 kg), chicken (1 kg), potatoes, apples, bananas, sugar, coffee, tea bags, beer (1 l), wine (1 l), vodka. MX: an everyday product in English or Spanish ('milk', 'eggs', 'tortilla', 'rice', 'beans', 'sugar', 'cooking oil', 'leche', 'huevo', 'frijol'). Profeco names products in Spanish with a pack size, so the answer names the exact product and pack and lists related ones. The 120 products priced in the most shops are held. MY: an everyday item in English or Malay ('chicken', 'eggs', 'rice', 'cooking oil', 'sugar', 'milk', 'onion', 'cabbage', 'ayam', 'telur'). DOSM names items in Malay with the pack size, so the answer names the exact item and lists related ones. Staples (chicken, eggs, rice, oil, flour, fish, fruit, vegetables, milk) and about 40 other well-covered items are held. WFP countries: a staple food in plain words ('rice', 'wheat flour', 'maize', 'beans', 'sugar', 'cooking oil', 'milk', 'onions', 'tomatoes', 'chicken'). WFP names foods its own way, e.g. 'Rice (high quality)'; the answer names the food and lists other definitions. Add 'wholesale' for wholesale prices, otherwise retail. US: the BLS's standard items, e.g. eggs (grade A large, per dozen), milk (whole, per gallon), bread (white pan bread, per lb), butter, cheddar cheese, chicken, ground beef, steak, bacon, bananas, oranges, potatoes, tomatoes, rice, pasta, flour, sugar, coffee (ground, per lb), soft drinks, beer, wine, ice cream. BLS has no tea or apples (dropped) and publishes most items per pound.

region.description: Region inside the country, only where the statistics office publishes regional averages. Leave out for the national average. Canada: leave out for the Canada average, or give a province (Ontario, BC, Quebec ...), Whitehorse (or Yukon) or Yellowknife (or Northwest Territories). A city such as Toronto is answered with its province's average. The two territories start in September 2025 and lack some products. GB: leave out for the whole UK, or give an English region (North East, North West, Yorkshire and the Humber, East Midlands, West Midlands, East of England, London, South East, South West), Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland (a big city maps to its region). ONS withholds a regional figure when fewer than ten observations stand behind it. HK: a supermarket chain ('Wellcome', 'ParknShop', 'Jasons', 'AEON'); leave out for all chains together. A chain needs 5 or more shelf prices in the category. IE: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. LV: national averages only; a region is ignored and the answer says so. MX: a state ('Jalisco', 'Nuevo Leon', 'Ciudad de Mexico', 'Yucatan', 'CDMX'); leave out for the national figure. A state needs 5 or more shops pricing the product. MY: a state ('Selangor', 'Johor', 'Sabah', 'Penang', 'Kuala Lumpur'); leave out for the national figure. A state needs 5 or more shops pricing the item. WFP countries: leave out. Figures are a spread across the country's surveyed markets. US: leave out for the U.S. city average, or give northeast, midwest, south or west (a US state maps to its region). BLS publishes no state or city averages for food.

name: pricepaid_grocery_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Official published index', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Posted or listed price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

title: Grocery and everyday prices
